blocks.title: First-Order RC Filter
blocks.body: A passive filter formed by a single resistor and capacitor. When output is taken across the capacitor, it forms a low-pass filter (LPF); when taken across the resistor, it forms a high-pass filter (HPF).

blocks.title: Cutoff Frequency and Transfer Function
blocks.tex: f_c = \frac{1}{2\pi R C}, \qquad H_{LP}(j\omega) = \frac{1}{1 + j\omega R C}
blocks.note: At cutoff frequency $\omega_c = 1/(RC)$, the gain is $-3\,\mathrm{dB}$ ($1/\sqrt{2} \approx 0.707$) and phase shift is $-45^\circ$.

blocks.title: High-Pass Transfer Function
blocks.tex: H_{HP}(j\omega) = \frac{j\omega R C}{1 + j\omega R C} = \frac{j(\omega/\omega_c)}{1 + j(\omega/\omega_c)}
blocks.note: Roll-off slope is $+20\,\mathrm{dB/decade}$ in the stopband below cutoff.

points: Cutoff frequency is independent of whether the circuit is configured as LPF or HPF.
Passband attenuation is $0\,\mathrm{dB}$ for ideal passive loading; real loads reduce passband gain.

questions: What is the total phase shift of a first-order low-pass filter at frequencies far above cutoff?
What happens to the cutoff frequency if a finite load resistance $R_L$ is placed across the capacitor?
